title: Animal Kingdom
syllabus: Salient features and classification of animals: Non-chordates up to phyla level (Porifera, Coelenterata, Ctenophora, Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata, Hemichordata) and Chordates up to classes level (Cyclostomata, Chondrichthyes, Osteichthyes, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia)

questions.question: Which of the following phyla possesses choanocytes (collar cells) lining the spongocoel and the canals?
questions.solution: Choanocytes or collar cells line the central spongocoel and radial canals in sponges (Phylum Porifera), maintaining a constant water current through the canal system for nutrition, respiration, and excretion.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the specialized excretory structures in animals:

List-I (Animal)List-II (Excretory Structure)
(A) Planaria(I) Malpighian tubules
(B) Pheretima (Earthworm)(II) Proboscis gland
(C) Locusta (Locust)(III) Flame cells (Protonephridia)
(D) Balanoglossus(IV) Nephridia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Planaria uses flame cells (protonephridia) for osmoregulation and excretion; Earthworm (Pheretima) uses nephridia; Locust (Locusta) uses Malpighian tubules; Balanoglossus (Hemichordata) has a proboscis gland.

questions.question: Metagenesis (alternation of generation between polyp and medusa forms) is exhibited by which of the following coelenterates?
questions.solution: In coelenterates like Obelia, metagenesis occurs: polyps produce medusae asexually, and medusae form polyps sexually.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding animal body symmetry and organization:

List-I (Phylum)List-II (Symmetry and Coelom)
(A) Platyhelminthes(I) Radial symmetry, acoelomate
(B) Aschelminthes(II) Bilateral symmetry, pseudocoelomate
(C) Annelida(III) Bilateral symmetry, acoelomate
(D) Adult Echinodermata(IV) Bilateral symmetry, true coelomate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Platyhelminthes: Bilateral, acoelomate; Aschelminthes: Bilateral, pseudocoelomate; Annelida: Bilateral, coelomate; Adult Echinodermata: Radial, coelomate.

questions.question: Bioluminescence (the property of a living organism to emit light) is well-marked and characteristic of which of the following phyla?
questions.solution: Ctenophores (comb jellies like Pleurobrachia and Ctenoplana) are exclusively marine, diploblastic, radially symmetrical organisms that prominently display bioluminescence.

questions.question: Which of the following animals is an acoelomate triploblastic bilaterian?
questions.solution: Platyhelminthes (e.g., Fasciola, Taenia) are the first triploblastic bilateral animals, and they are completely acoelomate (lacking a body cavity between gut and body wall).

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Aschelminthes:
Statement I: The body of aschelminthes is circular in cross-section, hence the name roundworms.
Statement II: An alimentary canal is complete with a well-developed muscular pharynx.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The body of Aschelminthes is circular in cross-section (roundworms), and they possess a complete digestive system featuring a characteristic well-developed muscular pharynx.

questions.question: Metameric segmentation (true body segment repetition externally and internally) is first observed in which phylum?
questions.solution: Metameric segmentation, where the body is divided into serial segments with serial repetition of at least some organs, is a hallmark characteristic first seen in Annelida (and also present in Arthropoda and Chordata).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the phylum Arthropoda and their functional representatives:

List-I (Type)List-II (Example)
(A) Economically important insect(I) Limulus (King crab)
(B) Vector of disease(II) Locusta (Locust)
(C) Gregarious pest(III) Anopheles (Mosquito)
(D) Living fossil(IV) Apis (Honey bee)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Economically important: Apis (Honey bee), Bombyx (Silkworm); Vector: Anopheles, Culex, Aedes; Gregarious pest: Locusta; Living fossil: Limulus (King crab).

questions.question: A rasping organ for feeding called 'radula' is found in which of the following phyla?
questions.solution: In molluscs (e.g., Pila, Sepia), the mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding called the radula.

questions.question: Water vascular system (ambulacral system) which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration is a unique diagnostic feature of:
questions.solution: The water vascular system is the most distinctive feature of Echinodermata (e.g., Asterias, Echinus), assisting in locomotion, food capture, transport, and respiration. (Note: Porifera has a water canal system, which is different).

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Phylum Hemichordata:
Statement I: The body of hemichordates is cylindrical and divided into an anterior proboscis, a collar, and a long trunk.
Statement II: They have an open circulatory system and respiration takes place through gills.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Hemichordates are marine, worm-like animals with a cylindrical body composed of a proboscis, collar, and trunk. They have an open circulatory system, gills for respiration, and a proboscis gland for excretion.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Subphyla of Chordates and their characteristics:

List-I (Subphylum)List-II (Notochord Extent / Feature)
(A) Urochordata(I) Notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life
(B) Cephalochordata(II) Notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in adults
(C) Vertebrata(III) Notochord is present only in larval tail

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: In Urochordata (e.g., Ascidia, Salpa), notochord is present only in the larval tail; in Cephalochordata (e.g., Branchiostoma), it extends from head to tail region and persists throughout life; in Vertebrata, it is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult.

questions.question: Which of the following classes of chordates contains jawless marine organisms with a sucking and circular mouth, lacking scales and paired fins?
questions.solution: Class Cyclostomata (Agnatha) includes jawless vertebrates (e.g., Petromyzon - Lamprey, Myxine - Hagfish) characterized by a circular, suctorial mouth without jaws, absence of scales, and absence of paired fins.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the comparison of Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes:

List-I (Class)List-II (Distinguishing Features)
(A) Chondrichthyes(I) Terminal mouth, 4 pairs of gills with operculum, air bladder present
(B) Osteichthyes(II) Ventral mouth, placoid scales, gill slits without operculum, claspers in males

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes) have ventral mouth, placoid scales, gill slits without operculum (except chimaeras), claspers on pelvic fins of males, and lack air bladder. Osteichthyes (bony fishes) have terminal mouth, cycloid/ctenoid scales, 4 pairs of operculated gills, and possess an air bladder for buoyancy.

questions.question: Which of the following cartilaginous fishes possesses a modified electric organ capable of delivering strong electric shocks to stun prey?
questions.solution: Torpedo (electric ray) possesses modified muscular electric organs that deliver strong electric shocks; Trygon (sting ray) possesses a venomous tail spine.

questions.question: A common chamber into which the alimentary canal, urinary, and reproductive tracts open in amphibians is called:
questions.solution: In Amphibia, the digestive tract, urinary system, and reproductive ducts all terminate into a common exterior chamber called the cloaca, which opens to the exterior.

questions.question: Which of the following reptiles possesses a FOUR-chambered heart (two atria and two ventricles)?
questions.solution: Reptiles generally have a 3-chambered heart (two atria and an incompletely divided ventricle), but crocodiles (Crocodilus, Alligator) are exceptions with a completely divided 4-chambered heart.

questions.question: Pneumatic bones (long bones that are hollow with air cavities) are an essential flight adaptation found in which class of vertebrates?
questions.solution: In birds (Class Aves), the endoskeleton is fully ossified (bony) and the long bones are pneumatic (hollow with air cavities) to reduce body weight for flight.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of characters are unique mammalian features not found in any other vertebrate class?
options: Mammary glands, body hair, and presence of pinnae (external ears)
Viviparity, 12 pairs of cranial nerves, and pulmonary respiration
Bony endoskeleton, cloaca, and heterodont dentition
questions.solution: Mammary glands (milk-producing glands for nourishing young), epidermal body hair, and external ear pinnae are exclusive diagnostic features of Class Mammalia.

questions.question: An oviparous (egg-laying) mammal is:
questions.solution: Ornithorhynchus (Duck-billed platypus) is a primitive, oviparous (egg-laying) prototherian mammal. Most other mammals (e.g., Macropus, Pteropus, Balaenoptera) are viviparous.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding animals and their common names:

List-I (Scientific Name)List-II (Common Name)
(A) Physalia(I) Sea anemone
(B) Pennatula(II) Portuguese man-of-war
(C) Gorgonia(III) Sea pen
(D) Adamsia(IV) Sea fan

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Physalia: Portuguese man-of-war; Pennatula: Sea pen; Gorgonia: Sea fan; Adamsia: Sea anemone.

questions.question: Eight external ciliary comb plates for locomotion and tentacles with colloblasts (lasso cells) are found in:
questions.solution: Pleurobrachia (Phylum Ctenophora) bears eight longitudinal rows of external ciliated comb plates that help in locomotion.

questions.question: Which of the following flatworms has a high capacity for regeneration?
questions.solution: Planaria (a free-living turbellarian flatworm) exhibits high regenerative capability (true regeneration).

questions.question: In Phylum Annelida, aquatic species like Nereis possess lateral appendages called ________ for swimming:
questions.solution: Aquatic annelids like Nereis possess unjointed, lateral fleshy appendages called parapodia which aid in swimming and gas exchange.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the respiratory organs in Arthropods:

List-I (Arthropod)List-II (Respiratory Organ)
(A) Prawn (Crustacean)(I) Book gills
(B) Limulus (King crab)(II) Tracheal system
(C) Scorpion / Spider(III) Gills
(D) Cockroach / Insects(IV) Book lungs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Prawns respire through gills; Limulus through book gills; Scorpions/spiders through book lungs; Cockroaches/insects through a branching tracheal system.

questions.question: The soft and spongy layer of skin that covers the visceral hump in molluscs is known as:
questions.solution: In molluscs, a soft and spongy layer of skin forms a mantle (pallium) over the visceral hump. The space between the hump and the mantle is the mantle cavity containing feather-like gills (ctenidia).

questions.question: Larval stages in Echinoderms show ________ symmetry, while adults exhibit ________ symmetry:
questions.solution: Adult echinoderms are radially (pentamerously) symmetrical, but their free-swimming ciliated larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.question: Which of the following chordate subphyla are collectively referred to as 'Protochordata' or 'Acrania'?
questions.solution: Subphyla Urochordata (Tunicata) and Cephalochordata are non-vertebrate chordates collectively called protochordates (or Acrania) and are exclusively marine.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Cyclostomes:
Statement I: Cyclostomes are marine but migrate for spawning to fresh water (anadromous migration).
Statement II: After spawning, within a few days, adult cyclostomes die, and their larvae return to the ocean after metamorphosis.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Marine cyclostomes (like Petromyzon) migrate to freshwater for spawning; adults die shortly after spawning, and their ammocoete larvae undergo metamorphosis and migrate back to the ocean.

questions.question: Which of the following fishes possesses an air bladder that regulates buoyancy and prevents the fish from sinking when not swimming?
questions.solution: Bony fishes (Osteichthyes, such as Labeo, Catla, Betta) possess an air bladder providing neutral buoyancy. Cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes, like Scoliodon) lack air bladders and must swim constantly to avoid sinking.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the scientific names of Osteichthyes (Bony fishes) and their common names:

List-I (Scientific Name)List-II (Common Name)
(A) Exocoetus(I) Fighting fish
(B) Hippocampus(II) Flying fish
(C) Betta(III) Sea horse
(D) Pterophyllum(IV) Angel fish

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Exocoetus: Flying fish; Hippocampus: Sea horse; Betta: Fighting fish; Pterophyllum: Angel fish.

questions.question: In Amphibians, the ear is represented by the external presence of:
questions.solution: Amphibians lack external ears (pinnae); the auditory organ on the body surface is represented by the tympanum.

questions.question: Reptiles are characterized as the first truly terrestrial vertebrates because of:
options: Dry, cornified skin covered by epidermal scales/scutes and cleidoic shelled eggs with internal fertilization
Presence of 4-chambered heart in all members
Ability to maintain constant body temperature (Homeothermy)
questions.solution: Reptiles adapted to dry terrestrial life by developing dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales/scutes, internal fertilization, and cleidoic (shelled) eggs that do not require water for development.

questions.question: In birds (Class Aves), which of the following digestive structures assist in storing and crushing/grinding food respectively?
questions.solution: The digestive tract of birds has additional chambers: the crop for food storage and the muscular gizzard for grinding food particles.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the scientific names and common names of Birds (Aves):

List-I (Scientific Name)List-II (Common Name)
(A) Neophron(I) Ostrich
(B) Struthio(II) Vulture
(C) Psittacula(III) Peacock
(D) Pavo(IV) Parrot

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Neophron: Vulture; Struthio: Ostrich; Psittacula: Parrot; Pavo: Peacock.

questions.question: Air sacs connected to lungs supplement respiration and make continuous unidirectional airflow possible in which class?
questions.solution: In Class Aves, lungs are spongy and inelastic; respiration is supplemented by connected internal air sacs, which also enhance buoyancy during flight.

questions.question: Which of the following animals is cold-blooded (Poikilothermic)?
questions.solution: Fishes, amphibians, and reptiles (such as Naja) are poikilothermic (cold-blooded), lacking internal physiological temperature regulation. Birds (Corvus, Columba) and mammals (Canis) are homeothermic (warm-blooded).

questions.question: Sponges reproduce asexually by ________ and sexually by formation of ________:
questions.solution: Sponges reproduce asexually by fragmentation (and internal budding via gemmules) and sexually by forming eggs and sperms (gametes). Fertilisation is internal and development is indirect via free-swimming ciliated larval stages.

questions.question: Cnidoblasts (stinging cells) present on the tentacles and body of Cnidarians are used for:
options: Anchorage, defense, and capture of prey
Circulation of nutrients throughout the body
questions.solution: Cnidoblasts (containing stinging capsules or nematocysts) serve three essential functions in cnidarians: anchorage to the substratum, defense against predators, and capturing prey.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the scientific names of Molluscs and their common names:

List-I (Mollusc)List-II (Common Name)
(A) Pila(I) Cuttlefish
(B) Pinctada(II) Apple snail
(C) Sepia(III) Pearl oyster
(D) Loligo(IV) Squid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Pila: Apple snail; Pinctada: Pearl oyster; Sepia: Cuttlefish; Loligo: Squid; Octopus: Devilfish.

questions.question: Which of the following is a limbless amphibian (Apoda)?
questions.solution: Ichthyophis is a limbless, burrowing amphibian belonging to order Gymnophiona (Apoda).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the fundamental diagnostic chordate characteristics and their non-chordate counterparts:

List-I (Chordate Feature)List-II (Non-chordate Condition)
(A) Notochord(I) Absent
(B) Central Nervous System (CNS)(II) Ventral, solid and double
(C) Pharyngeal gill slits(III) Absent
(D) Heart(IV) Dorsal (if present)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: In Chordates: Notochord present, CNS is dorsal, hollow and single, pharynx perforated by gill slits, heart is ventral. In Non-chordates: Notochord absent, CNS is ventral, solid and double, gill slits absent, heart is dorsal (if present).

questions.question: Which of the following is an aquatic mammalian species that exhibits viviparity and breathes through lungs?
questions.solution: Dolphins (Delphinus) and blue whales (Balaenoptera) are secondary aquatic placental mammals with pulmonary respiration, homeothermy, mammary glands, and viviparity.

questions.question: In which of the following animals does the skin serve as an accessory respiratory organ throughout life in terrestrial and aquatic environments?
questions.solution: Frogs (Rana tigrina) perform cutaneous respiration through their thin, highly vascularized, moist, and scaleless skin both in water and on land (during hibernation and aestivation).
